### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/rest`, touching **2** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via registerMetaCollectionRoutes (symbol, a top-level function))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **58** of **210** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **19** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2a3dec2d498ea8467460f07dd3fb0e46ddc3cf8d` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `75677847d69df8a378b48871d8854f0db5ecf08a` — the merge of head `2e2306d961bb53b442887ab410252f8ccf204661` into base `2a3dec2d498ea8467460f07dd3fb0e46ddc3cf8d`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 75677847d69df8a378b48871d8854f0db5ecf08a && git checkout 75677847d69df8a378b48871d8854f0db5ecf08a
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 2a3dec2d498ea8467460f07dd3fb0e46ddc3cf8d 2e2306d961bb53b442887ab410252f8ccf204661 && git checkout -B drift-repro 2a3dec2d498ea8467460f07dd3fb0e46ddc3cf8d && git merge --no-ff 2e2306d961bb53b442887ab410252f8ccf204661

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2a3dec2d498ea8467460f07dd3fb0e46ddc3cf8d
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 2a3dec2d498ea8467460f07dd3fb0e46ddc3cf8d` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

### ① Derived judgments

- Face: narrowing (`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` on PR body and changeset; `Metadata-protocol: none`; `Skills-docs: follow-up #27632`, addition posted as comment 6514340216). Matches card #27633 and triage 6501809473. No schema, no governed path in the 3-file diff.
- **Closed set = `type`, `severity`, `package`** — exactly the handler's read points (`req.query?.severity` L324, `?.type` L331, `?.package` L341 via `metaItemPackageBinding`). No paging/format/sort on this route. Nothing reads the query before the handler: `resolveProtocol` and `resolveExecCtx` read none; `metaRequestLocale` (`?locale=`) is not called on this route; no auth middleware query read found in `packages/rest/src`.
- Consumers send only the set: SDK `client.meta.getDiagnostics` (`packages/client/src/index.ts:2210`, `packageId` opt → `package` wire), Console `metadata-client.diagnostics` (`ui/.../metadata-client.ts:1805`, same three), `useMetadata.ts` calls through it; CLI does not call the route; docs table (`validating-metadata.mdx:807-811`) and route ledger name the same three; every `diagnostics?…` string in the repo uses `type=`/`severity=`/`package=` only. Nothing a real caller sends is now refused.
- Refusal ordering: unknown name is thrown before `refuseRepeatedQueryParams`, before the severity check and before `getMetaDiagnostics` — no sweep work precedes it (only `resolveProtocol` and the 501 capability check, which are prerequisites, not the sweep). Test pins unknown-name-outranks-repeat.
- Deviation (decision helper + route envelope): `unknownQueryParamRefusalMessage` is the documented seam for "a door with its own envelope" (query-allowlist.ts docblock, #23072); precedents `metaItemQueryRefusal` (meta-item-read-gate.ts:2444) and `package-routes.ts:502` (#26857) do the same. Message is byte-identical to the fleet sentence; code `INVALID_REQUEST` is what card, triage and the route's #27514 one-envelope rule prescribe. Correct.
- Residual: a repeated known parameter still answers `VALIDATION_ERROR` (pre-existing #6877 path, untouched). Disclosed in PR body/changeset and in the #27632 addition. Non-blocking: the #27514 "one envelope" claim is about the nested shape, which holds; the two codes are both ledgered members. Could be folded later under #27632's docs card or a tiny follow-up if the seat wants one code per route.
- Tests: 5 new cases through the registered handler (real protocol over real registry), red-on-main per PR body; preservation pin keeps the three names answering 200 together.
- Checks at review time: 27 success (incl. Check Changeset, Lint & Repo Gates, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Test Core 8/8), 13 skipped, Test Core shards 1–7 of 8 still in progress — seat waits for green before landing.

### ② Semver level

- `@objectstack/rest: patch` — correct: `Metadata-protocol: none` ⇒ patch; a narrowing ships patch with its BREAKING banner (AGENTS.md step 3). Banner present in changeset and PR body with the remedy (drop the parameter / `package` not `packageId`).
- ADR-0087: exactly one marker, `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, a `CATEGORIES` member of `scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs`; reasoning (request-side only, nothing stored to rewrite) holds. Same disposition as the merged sibling #27620.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Nested `{ error: { code, message } }` envelope (ADR-0112) kept; message bounded by `truncateClientMessage`.
- `packages/spec` untouched; no new error code; route ledger row unchanged (response schema unaffected).
- `META_DIAGNOSTICS_PARAMS` is module-private; the ingress policy text says "an exported `readonly string[]`" — nit only, no consumer needs it.
- Branch is the thread's platform-assigned `claude/project-thread-lmg708` (recorded exception in the claim).

### ④ Design judgment

- Against the published spec on `main` (docs table, ledger, both SDKs): the narrowing takes no declared capability away — every documented and SDK-sent parameter stays accepted — and makes the route's own refusal real for the false-all-clear #27514 left open on the name axis. Holds against the cited code and the card's scenario (`?typ=view` → 400 naming `"typ"` and listing the set).

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-lmg708`
Reviewed-by: `session_016WV4czuTWNgKR22fKv7jia (seat subagent)`

**VERDICT: PASS**
